question.text: The number of $3 \times 3$ matrices $A$ whose entries are either 0 or 1 and for which the system $A\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$ has exactly two distinct solutions, is

solution.text:
Since, $A\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$ is linear equation in three variables and that could have only unique, no solution or infinitely many solution.
$\therefore$ It is not possible to have two solutions.
Hence, number of matrices $A$ is zero.
